change: Write each uncompressed MySQL frame through borrowed header/body IoSlices. Forward ClientStream vectored writes to TCP or a borrowed rustls::Stream over the existing TLS owner. runtime_red.protocol_evidence: A three-byte payload reaches the old transport in two scalar calls instead of one vectored frame call.
runtime_red.tls_evidence: The old ClientStream default vectored implementation accepts only the first slice, 7 of 16 bytes. This is valid Write behavior but loses the intended coalescing.

validation.compile_correction: The first post-change attempt used ErrorKind.into() where PacketError requires io::Error. Corrected the conversion; that compile failure is not behavioral regression evidence.

after.build_note: 0.26-second final build reused the candidate artifacts compiled during the 1m56s TLS test build.

live.coverage: Seven cases per plaintext/TLS endpoint across Go, before and after: PING, scalar/large/range results, error packets, affected-row OK and staged read followed by rollback. TLS socket cipher/version match SHOW SESSION STATUS. Eleven overlay and 48 DISTINCT/HAVING cases per endpoint; three DISTINCT errors are expected Go errors. Physical plans are not claimed equal.
live.tls_policy: Live endpoints use local self-signed certificates, so this helper tests encryption without certificate identity verification. The independent Rust TLS test trusts and verifies its generated certificate. No server TLS policy changed.

sysbench.interpretation: Two of three candidate pairs are slower despite a positive median. This does not establish a reliable sysbench gain.

tpcc.interpretation: All five transaction types and exact counts completed in every sample. All six candidate pairs are slower. Shared evolving data and time-seeded mixes limit attribution, but do not justify dismissing the regressions.

command_diagnostic.interpretation: PING isolates the single OK frame without SQL/TiKV work; SELECT 1 controls the already-batched result path. Each short sample is 5,000 fixed data-free commands. PING medians improve but all groups have mixed pair directions; the unchanged result-batch control also varies. This does not establish a stable latency gain or explain the TPC-C regression.

after_profile.interpretation: The workload traverses the new vectored path. Earlier unpaired type-read diagnostics used Rust/TiKV 56.14/141.73 CPU-seconds over 36.00s, versus 55.31/162.44 over 38.66s now. Different time-seeded mixes and evolving data prevent attributing throughput changes to these counters. Non-wait inclusive frame counts are not CPU percentages; do not use them as a causal gain receipt.
after_profile.postcheck_commands: Same two commands as postcheck.commands, repeated after profiling
